answer: One-person reward credentials. An agent planning a voyage to survey lotus habitats must present a credential from a registry that checks each human controller once. The verifier derives an epoch nullifier from that credential and rejects a second claim with the same nullifier, even from another account. N hollow identities controlled by one person still receive one reward quota; N quotas require recruiting N distinct people and paying their participation costs. This relies on reliable deduplication; credential rental can defeat it.
